benchmark.baseline: Pre-encoding physical-namespace index with BTreeSet<&Path>, minimal covering frontier and one-pass Components iterator; saved at /tmp/recovery-resources-before-encoded.rs. Baseline harness only rewrites its test include to an absolute path.
benchmark.measurement: Five alternating fresh processes per variant; Rust Instant around index construction; Linux wait4 ru_maxrss for peak process KiB. Raw outputs /tmp/recovery-resource-{baseline,encoded}-sample-{0..4}.log.
benchmark.limits: Whole-process RSS includes fixture/runtime. Shared-host scheduling and a Clippy run overlapped some late samples; not a controlled device benchmark or statistically established tail latency. Encoded key storage trades additional memory for comparison cost. No app startup or ordinary mutation latency claim.

limitations: Resource capture remains Unix-only; Windows per-directory case/short-name and provider semantics and case-insensitive macOS volumes remain required
Production callers still do not acquire recovery reservations; durable replacement/reconciliation/IPC/UI/Undo/retention and full platform acceptance remain incomplete
The resource-record byte budget does not claim a strict bound on total allocator overhead across all journal records
No publication, Windows runtime, macOS half-bounce measurement or release acceptance this checkpoint
